lyrics:
[Intro: spoken count, picked three-chord guitar figure, bass, drums]
One, two, three
Louder

[Verse 1: easy drawl, guitar figure throughout]
Wheels are humming on the two-lane back
Past the grain elevator and the railroad track
I've been to cities where they don't say hi
I'm coming home to the widest sky

[Chorus: female backing singers answer, piano rolling]
Sweet nowhere special
Where the map runs out of names
Sweet nowhere special
It's exactly where I aim

[Verse 2: easy drawl, a grin in it]
Well, I heard a fella on the TV say
Nothing ever happens out our way
I hope that fella takes a drive some time
A whole lot of nothing suits us fine

[Chorus: female backing singers answer, piano rolling]
Sweet nowhere special
Where the map runs out of names
Sweet nowhere special
It's exactly where I aim

[Guitar Solo: bright, country-tinged, bending notes]

[Verse 3: easy drawl, band cooking]
Now the diner's got a house band Thursday nights
A drummer and a dentist and a set of lights
They play it loose and they play it loud
And the whole of the county makes a pretty good crowd

[Chorus: female backing singers answer, piano rolling]
Sweet nowhere special
Where the map runs out of names
Sweet nowhere special
It's exactly where I aim

[Piano Solo: honky-tonk, rolling]

[Final Chorus: everyone, backing singers ad-libbing]
Sweet nowhere special
(Ooh, where the sky's that wide)
Sweet nowhere special
It's exactly where I aim

[Outro: guitar figure, piano, backing singers, fade]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 98 BPM, 4/4, G major. A loping, relaxed Southern rock groove. Sunny and sure of itself.

VOICE: Male, with an easy, slightly nasal Southern drawl and a conversational, unhurried delivery. Three female backing singers with a gospel-soul sound answer his lines in the chorus and improvise in the last one. A spoken count at the top.

INSTRUMENTS: An electric guitar playing a bright, picked three-chord figure with a small fill at the end of each bar, repeating throughout. Two more guitars adding rhythm and a country-tinged lead with bent notes. A honky-tonk piano rolling under everything and taking a solo. A bouncing bass. A relaxed drum kit with a strong backbeat.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, a spoken count and the guitar figure. 0:16 Verse 1. 0:36 Chorus 1. 0:56 Verse 2. 1:16 Chorus 2. 1:36 Guitar solo. 2:00 Verse 3. 2:20 Chorus 3. 2:40 Piano solo. 3:04 Final chorus with ad-libs. 3:30 Outro, the figure and piano fading by 3:55.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Mid-1970s Southern rock: warm, loose and live-sounding, three guitars spread across the stereo field, piano and backing voices bright.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The guitar figure after the spoken 'Louder' at 0:04.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The quarrel in the original is with a famous songwriter. Here it is with a voice on television, and the answer is an invitation. The house band with a dentist in it is the detail only someone who went home would know.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Homesickness, a friendly bristle, contentment.
